report_name: Berlin Government Defies Rhysida Ransomware After 5.79TB Data Theft

threat_actors.name: Rhysida
threat_actors.description: A ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group that emerged in mid-2023, known for double-extortion tactics. The group compromised the network of a Berlin Senate Department, exfiltrated 5.79 TB of data, and is auctioning it on their darknet leak site. Security researchers believe the group may have ties to Russia or Eastern Europe.
threat_actors.goals: To extort the city government of Berlin for a ransom payment of 30 bitcoin by threatening to leak 5.79 TB of stolen data.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Rhysida ransomware encrypted files, indicated by the hunting hint to look for files with the `.rhysida` extension.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors exfiltrated 5.79 TB of data from the city's administrative network between August 7 and August 12, 2026.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: Rhysida was observed using PowerShell for lateral movement and payload execution within the compromised network.

malware.name: Rhysida
malware.description: A ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) payload used to encrypt files on the Berlin government network. It creates ransom notes named 'Critical_Message.pdf' and appends the '.rhysida' extension to encrypted files.

identities.name: Berlin state government
identities.description: The state government of Berlin, Germany, which was the target of the Rhysida ransomware attack and extortion demand.

identities.name: Senate Department for Mobility, Transport, Climate Protection and Environment
identities.description: The specific department within the Berlin state government from which 5.79 TB of data was exfiltrated.

infrastructure.name: Rhysida Darknet Leak Site
infrastructure.description: The darknet site used by the Rhysida group to auction the 5.79 TB of data stolen from the Berlin government.

indicators.name: Rhysida Ransom Note File IOC
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Rhysida Ransom Note Creation
id: 7c5b9f8a-1d2e-4c3b-a1f0-9e8d7c6b5a4d
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of the Rhysida ransom note file 'Critical_Message.pdf'.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/berlin-refuses-to-pay-hackers-who-stole.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-29
tags:
  - attack.t1486
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\Critical_Message.pdf'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of the Rhysida ransomware group's known ransom note file, 'Critical_Message.pdf'.

indicators.name: Rhysida Encrypted File Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Rhysida Encrypted File Detected
id: 8b4a8e7d-2c1f-4b2a-9f8e-7d6c5b4a3d2e
status: experimental
description: Detects files being renamed with the .rhysida extension, indicating Rhysida ransomware activity.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/berlin-refuses-to-pay-hackers-who-stole.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-29
tags:
  - attack.t1486
level: critical
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.rhysida'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects files being created or renamed with the `.rhysida` extension, which is characteristic of the Rhysida ransomware.

indicators.name: Rhysida PowerShell Execution Pattern
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution Policy Bypass
id: 9a3d7c6b-1f0e-4d2c-8b4a-6c5b4a3d2e1f
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of PowerShell with the ExecutionPolicy Bypass flag, a technique observed with Rhysida for lateral movement and payload execution.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/berlin-refuses-to-pay-hackers-who-stole.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-29
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -ExecutionPolicy Bypass '
      - ' -Exec Bypass '
      - ' -ep Bypass '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects suspicious PowerShell execution with a bypassed execution policy, a TTP associated with the Rhysida group.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Data Exfiltration
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Outbound Data Transfer
id: a0b9c8d7-3e2f-4a1b-9c8d-7e6f5d4c3b2a
status: experimental
description: Detects large, sustained data transfers to external addresses, which could indicate data exfiltration as performed by groups like Rhysida.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/berlin-refuses-to-pay-hackers-who-stole.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-29
tags:
  - attack.t1041
level: low
logsource:
  category: network_traffic
detection:
  selection:
    BytesOut|gt: 1000000000 # 1GB
  timeframe: 1h
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Identifies large, sustained outbound data transfers, which could be indicative of data exfiltration activity similar to that described in the Rhysida attack.
